messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGE: Cache correctness alert for KV prefix routing (prod-us-east-1). Severity: P1. Alert: sustained divergence between primary KV and prefix cache; automated prefix-checker flipping to safemode. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/cache-correctness

Alyssa: I'm on the page. seeing 3x increase in customer-reported mismatches and a spike in 'stale_read' signals. hopping into the nodes now.

Sam: Confirmed. Traffic shows normal latency but responses sometimes contain older embeddings/metadata. Error rate for correctness checks ~8% on the affected prefix cohort.

Mohit: Root cause appears to be a partial snapshot lag on the sync pipeline + TTL expiry leading to stale prefixes being served. We need correctness, so plan: enable prefix-level bypass to read directly from primary KV for impacted tenant prefixes, plus soft rate caps to avoid hammering primary.

Lina: Agreed. Immediate actions I propose: 1) enable bypass for prefix set P{a-f} (low-cardinality hot set) 2) apply per-tenant emergency rate limit to 20rps for those tenants 3) reduce global batch size to 8 to lower KV pressure.

Jen: +1. also recommend temporarily disabling prefetch for affected shards to avoid further pollution of cache.

Alyssa: I'm going to run the bypass toggle now. tagging @oncall for handoff if this goes beyond 30m.

ops-bot: Command executed: set_prefix_bypass --prefixes P001,P002,P003 --mode=direct_read --scope=prod-us-east-1 --initiated-by=Alyssa

Sam: Applying per-tenant emergency quota policy. snippet:
```
policy:
  name: emergency-prefix-ratecap
  scope: tenants:[T-44,T-108,T-209]
  rate: 20 rps
  burst: 40
```

Mohit: Running a quick sanity curl to the control plane to confirm bypass is active:
```
curl -X POST "https://controlplane.internal/v1/flags/prefix_bypass" \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN' \
  -d '{"prefixes": ["P001","P002","P003"], "mode": "direct_read"}'
```

Alyssa: Verified bypass active. Logs show direct reads to primary up from 2% -> 28% of requests for those prefixes. Early correctness check: mismatch rate down from 8% -> 0.9% for tested keys.

Customer Success: We have 3 customers affected (tenant IDs in policy). Drafting a short heads-up to send to them: "We're investigating reads that returned stale data. We've enabled a temporary correctness bypass and applied protective rate limits. We will follow up with timeline and root cause." Want to review before send.

Lina: Good. Also adding monitoring alert to watch primary KV latency. If primary P99 > 400ms for 2min, auto-scale primary read pool and widen rate caps.

Jen: I pushed a temporary traffic-sculpt rule to smooth bursts:
```
traffic_sculpt:
  region: prod-us-east-1
  algorithm: leaky_bucket
  rate: 200 rps
  burst: 50
```

Alyssa: Noted increased read latency on primary after bypass toggled (P95 ~180ms, P99 ~560ms) — Lina, do we want to widen the per-tenant cap further or pause bypass?

Lina: Pause bypass if primary P99 stays > 500ms for > 3 minutes. For now reduce bypass scope: limit to prefixes observed in customer complaints only (P001,P003). Apply that now.

ops-bot: Command executed: set_prefix_bypass --prefixes P001,P003 --mode=direct_read --scope=prod-us-east-1 --initiated-by=Lina

Sam: Adjusted per-tenant quotas: T-209 reduced to 10rps (was 20), T-44 stays at 20rps, T-108 at 15rps.

Alyssa: Handing off to Lina for next shift — my pager quiets in ~25 minutes. Lina, you have it. @oncall please ack.

oncall: acked. taking handoff at 2026-03-15T21:12:00Z. will monitor for 45m.

Mohit: Quick note on telemetry: saved sample queries and a snapshot of mismatched keys (obfuscated) to the incident bucket for postmortem: s3://redwood-incidents/2186504321/samples.json.gz

Customer Success: Sent initial messages to affected customers. Two replies asking for ETA; responded with "investigation in progress, temporary correctness bypass applied, expect follow-up in 4 hours."

Alyssa: We're seeing correctness stabilize across the three tenants at 21:08 UTC. Primary P99 trending down to ~320ms after reducing scope and rate caps.

Lina: Plan for next steps: 1) keep bypass limited and rate-capped for 2 hours 2) rehydrate prefix cache after fix is deployed 3) schedule postmortem and link to infra PR that will fix the snapshot lag. I'll draft comms for status.redwood.

Jen: Adding a mitigation checklist item for the runbook: prefer scoped bypass + per-tenant quotas before global bypass to protect primary.

ops-bot: Incident note appended to ticket INC-2186504321. Next: create postmortem doc and assign owners.

Alyssa: Thanks team. Lina, if you need more capacity from infra (read pool), ping me and I'll escalate.

Lina: Will do. monitoring set. I'll tidy up the thread and capture timeline for the postmortem.

incident-bot: Incident escalated to P1 -> P0 review required for postmortem. Add timeline and customer IDs to internal doc.

Customer Success: After messaging, all three customers acknowledged and appreciate proactive notice. closing loop once postmortem ready.

Lina: closing the live mitigation phase at 21:32 UTC — moving to mitigation verification. Will update ticket when we start cache rehydration.

Alyssa: Good job all."
